WHAT: publishAdminFundVersion takes an optional expectedVersion as a QUERY parameter (convention-12): POST /v1/admin/funds/{fundId}/versions?expectedVersion=N. Released backends ignore the query, so a newer admin APK keeps publishing after a rollback.

The backend locks the fund row, compares the value with fund.currentVersion, and refuses a mismatch with 409 STATE_CONFLICT plus fields.expectedVersion. This runs inside the idempotent transaction, so a refusal writes nothing, and an accepted key resent later replays. Without the query, the publish and its request hash are unchanged. The response is unchanged.
Admin app: the form starts from, and sends, the version the fund points to. A stale refusal shows a plain 'Not published' line with Reload the fund, and Check again keeps the same key and query.
DEPLOY.md: the rollback behaviour of the query parameter, plus the Not confirmed clause for a publish that reached the server across a rollback or roll-forward.

WHAT: publishAdminFundVersion takes an optional expectedVersion. The backend takes the fund row lock (the same select ... for update the publish already used), reads the fund's current terms version (fund.currentVersion), and refuses a mismatch with 409 STATE_CONFLICT before any write. The error carries fields.expectedVersion and a plain message.

WHERE IT TRAVELS: a QUERY parameter, POST /v1/admin/funds/{fundId}/versions?expectedVersion=N, not a body key. Every released backend (v0.15.4, v0.17.0, v0.18.0) parses this body with .strict(), so a body key would be refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. But the publish route never reads request.query, so the query is ignored there. Rule 11 and step 5: the new admin app keeps publishing against the previous backend. The name matches the other operations' expectedVersion.

Contract: AdminFundVersionPublishQuery (strict, coerce int > 0, optional) in admin-fund-aum.ts (788 lines). OpenAPI regenerated. No new error code: STATE_CONFLICT was already in this operation's errorCodes, is how the other expected-version checks refuse (VERSION_CONFLICT maps to it, as does the app-config publish), and is shown as a plain 'Not published' refusal by the v0.15.4 and v0.18.0 admin screens. Response shape unchanged.

Atomic: the check runs inside runAdminMutation's transaction, after the idempotency claim and the lock. A refusal rolls back and writes no version, disclosure, audit row or idempotency receipt. Resending an accepted request with its key replays it (201) instead of refusing it as stale.

Released apps (rule 11, finding-14): they send no query, so the publish runs as before. The request hash adds expectedVersion only when it is present, so receipts stored before the deploy still replay. A strict query means a stray query key on this route is now 400; no client sends one.

Admin app: PublishTermsSection sends the start.version the form was built on, when start.kind is found. For kind none (a fund with no terms, which createFund cannot produce) nothing is sent and the server does not check. The held body includes expectedVersion, so Check again resends the same key and the same query, and an unknown outcome stays Not confirmed (FX-4, the existing ROWS test compares the full options).

On the refusal it shows 'Not published': 'Newer terms were published for this fund after this form was opened, so nothing was published. Reload the fund to see them; your edits stay in the form.', with a Reload the fund button. After the reload, the existing 'A newer version was published' alert takes over, prefixed 'Nothing was published.', with 'Start again from version N', which also resets the refusal. The archived-fund STATE_CONFLICT keeps its old text. The screen-side re-read before sending is kept: it is the only check against an older backend.

DEPLOY.md: one paragraph under Database rollback semantics. From 0.18.1 the version travels as a query parameter. After an images-only rollback a newer admin APK still publishes, checked only by its own re-read, as in 0.18.0.

WHAT: publishAdminFundVersion takes an optional expectedVersion as a QUERY parameter (convention-12): POST /v1/admin/funds/{fundId}/versions?expectedVersion=N. Released backends parse the body strictly but ignore the query, so a newer admin APK keeps publishing after a rollback.

The backend locks the fund row, reads fund.currentVersion (the version current_published_version_id points to), and refuses a mismatch with 409 STATE_CONFLICT plus fields.expectedVersion. This runs inside the idempotent transaction, so a refusal writes nothing, and an accepted key resent later replays.
Compatibility: without the query, the publish and its request hash are unchanged (released apps and stored receipts). The response is unchanged. No new error code.

Admin app (after e66c866): the form starts from the version the fund points to, not the newest entry of versions, and sends that version. A fund with versions but no current pointer reads as unreadable, and the form is hidden; createFund cannot make one. Check again keeps the same key and query.

On a stale refusal it shows 'Not published: Newer terms were published for this fund after this form was opened...' with Reload the fund. After the reload, the existing 'A newer version was published' notice offers 'Start again from version N'.

DEPLOY.md, under Database rollback semantics: the query parameter and the rollback behaviour. A publish that reached the server and was left Not confirmed across a rollback or roll-forward stays Not confirmed on Check again (the request hashes differ), so check the fund's versions by hand.
